subject.title: fix(auth-profiles): import legacy auth-profiles.json into SQLite store on load

question: Should OpenClaw allow normal runtime auth loads to import retired secret-bearing `auth-profiles.json`, or must this recovery stay in a doctor/update/startup migration boundary?
rationale: The PR fixes a real upgrade symptom, but the chosen layer changes the credential migration and runtime trust boundary that current policy, docs, and tests treat as doctor-owned.

options.title: Keep runtime SQLite-only
options.body: Rework this PR toward a doctor/update/startup migration or loud startup diagnostic and leave normal auth reads from the canonical SQLite store only.

options.title: Approve runtime fallback
options.body: Accept the runtime import only with explicit maintainer approval plus updated invariant tests, docs, and security expectations for legacy credential JSON.

options.title: Resolve through canonical issue
options.body: Pause this branch and use the broader related issue to decide the stranded-profile migration and fallback-chain diagnostic behavior together.

recommendation.title: Keep runtime SQLite-only
recommendation.body: Rework this PR toward a doctor/update/startup migration or loud startup diagnostic and leave normal auth reads from the canonical SQLite store only.

likelyOwner.reason: The history points to steipete as the strongest owner for the SQLite auth-store boundary and the repository policy question around runtime versus doctor migration.
